answer: One strong Sybil defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a garden that only grows where a gardener has planted real seed. An attacker spawning hundreds of fake identities must fund each one, so the cost scales linearly while the reward does not. If two identities are ever proven to share one operator, both stakes are slashed, turning the attack into a loss. Like nectar that draws only real pollinators, the reward flows to identities with something at stake, while a zephyr of cheap fakes passes through without settling.
